title: Video Editor Roadmap
summary: Build a career in video editing by developing storytelling, editing, sound, colour correction, motion graphics and delivery skills, then progress toward senior editing, post-production supervision or independent production.

facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – New Media / Digital Media
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a three-year bachelor's degree, with an optional fourth-year honours route where offered. The horizons extend from 2026 to 2046. Career progression and salary outcomes depend on portfolio quality, employer demand, specialisation and experience.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: A showreel, editing portfolio and experience through internships, freelance projects or junior editing work.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Expertise in a chosen area such as short-form content, documentaries, advertising, films or branded video.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Senior editing responsibilities, post-production supervision, creative direction or a specialist freelance business.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Leadership or independent work combining creative judgement, efficient workflows and emerging production technology.

blocks.text: Horizon outputs are planning targets;

blocks.text: If your university offers a fourth year, use it for an advanced film, research-led media project or specialist editing portfolio. Confirm the degree structure and requirements with your institution.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move beyond operating editing software to making stronger creative decisions, managing complex projects, guiding teams and improving post-production workflows. Learn AI-assisted editing while retaining control over factual accuracy, copyright, consent, visual consistency and final quality.

Career progression

blocks.label: Year 1–2
blocks.text: Student Editor / Editing Intern

blocks.label: Year 3–5
blocks.text: Junior Video Editor / Assistant Editor

blocks.label: Year 5–9
blocks.text: Video Editor / Specialist Editor

blocks.label: Year 9–14
blocks.text: Senior Editor / Post-Production Supervisor

blocks.label: Year 14+
blocks.text: Editing Director / Post-Production Head / Studio Owner
The progression is illustrative; freelancers may follow a different path and can develop a client business without holding every intermediate job title.
PhD routes
A PhD is not required for professional video editing. It may be relevant if your long-term goal includes teaching, research or media scholarship.

2040–2046: remain relevant. Develop expertise in visual storytelling, colour, sound, accessibility, copyright and project leadership. AI will continue to change editing workflows, but creative judgement, narrative coherence, visual consistency and responsible handling of source material remain important. Build a career around the value you deliver rather than a single editing application.
